\begin{abstract}
\noindent We run the released Jacobian-lens evaluations (6 sets) and
experiment prompt sets (11 sets) from the public companion release of
``Verbalizable Representations Form a Global Workspace in Language
Models'' under one audited harness on two open-weight models, and
separate prompt, lens, intervention, capability, and model effects.
Both lanes are complete: Qwen 3.6 27B under the campaign-validated
published $n{=}1000$ lens (OR-Q1/Q2), and OLMo 3.1 32B Instruct under
one prospectively fitted, fit-stable $n{=}250$ official-estimator lens
(OR-Q3), closed by a bounded instrument cross-over (OR-Q4). Headline:
released \emph{readout} contrasts reproduce directionally on both
models (selectivity exactly); the paper-literal \emph{coordinate
interventions} transfer weakly and concordantly ($\sim$5--30\% vs the
paper's 40--88\%, with the $\alpha{=}2$ remedy inverting); and the
campaign's broad protected J-suppression is selectively destructive on
the official prompts of both lanes while matched controls are not ---
the two intervention families estimate different causal questions.
Fidelity classes and gate states are carried on every cell; gated
cells are missing, never zero; no confirmatory language is licensed
anywhere in Study 1.
\end{abstract}

\section{Qwen causal core (OR-Q2)}

\subsection{Verbal report}
Release-literal rule (first ten listed candidates, skip the answer),
swap-out = greedy token at the generation boundary (D1), $\alpha{=}1$
across the band at every prompt position. \textbf{Primary numbers are
the v2 rerun} (\texttt{or1-qwen-verbal-report-v2}): category-equal
top-1 \qwvrvtwocattopone{} and top-5 \qwvrvtwocattopfive{}
(\qwvrvtwonexec{} executed trials; \qwvrvtwoimproved{} improved /
\qwvrvtwoworsened{} worsened). Paper context (Claude): 88\% top-5.

\textbf{Incident or1-001 (resolved):} the superseded v1 run scored the
leading-space token form at a boundary whose in-context form is bare
and reported top-5 \qwvrcattopfive{} --- i.e.\ \emph{three quarters of
the apparent Qwen verbal-report deficit was a scoring-form artifact}
(the model's top-1 literally became \texttt{Red} while the scored
\texttt{\textvisiblespace Red} form sat at rank 5). v2 scores min over
both single-token forms with the boundary in-context swap vector; OLMo
ran v2 semantics from its first execution. See
\texttt{reports/INCIDENT\_or1-001\_vr\_token\_form.md}.

\section{Worked examples: what the swaps actually do}

The aggregate rates hide a bimodal reality worth seeing item by item.
When the paper-literal swap works on Qwen, it works emphatically — the
predicted counterfactual answer jumps hundreds of ranks to top-1:

\begin{table}[h]\centering\small
\qwpswinstable
\caption{The \qwpsnwins{} probe-swap successes (of 63 baseline-capable
items), largest baseline distance first. \texttt{ex2-city-capital-Munich}:
swapping the J-lens vector Munich$\to$(released target) at every prompt
position moves the predicted capital from rank 122 to the model's
literal output. One success (\texttt{rhyme-rain-neighbor}) was already
rank 1 before the swap (\qwpsnwinstrivial{} such trivial cell in the
count); \qwpsnnear{} further items land in the top-5 without reaching
top-1 — the modal failure is \emph{under-strength}, not wrong-direction.}
\end{table}

\begin{table}[h]\centering\small
\qwfgwinstable
\caption{The \qwfgnwins{} flexible-generalization $\alpha{=}1$ successes
concentrate in the \emph{countries} category (capable top-1 23.3\%
there): \texttt{capital Egypt$\to$Canada} drives \texttt{Ottawa} from
rank 480 to the output. Months and numbers show none — the four
released categories differ enormously, exactly the per-category
variance the paper's own appendix warns about.}
\end{table}

Two structural observations. First, successes cluster where the
swapped-in argument has a strong, single-token, high-frequency identity
(cities, countries, elements); the sparse-identity categories (months
as time-words, small numbers) never flip. Second, the near-miss mass
(top-5 but not top-1) plus the incident-or1-001 form effect mean the
honest Qwen picture is ``the mechanism visibly engages but rarely
completes the flip at $\alpha{=}1$'' — which makes the $\alpha{=}2$
\emph{reversal} (0\% capable) the more interesting anomaly: on Qwen the
doubled patch overshoots into off-distribution territory rather than
completing near-misses, unlike the paper's Sonnet where $\alpha{=}2$
lifted 76/192 to 101/192.

\section{OR1-B: the OLMo official-estimator fit}

Timing gate (frozen before any outcome): dim\_batch ladder
161/164/181/232/386\,s per prompt for 16/8/4/2/1 $\Rightarrow$
dim\_batch=\olfitdimbatch{} at \olfitsperprompt{}\,s/prompt; only the
2$\times$125 tier fits the 18\,GPU-hour ceiling $\Rightarrow$ merged
$n{=}\olfitmerged$ (the addendum's honest-prior tier). Both halves
completed 125/125 with zero skips. Split-half operator audit: median
symmetric relative Frobenius \olshmedfrob{} across the 32 fitted layers
(\olshbandfrob{} in-band); minus-identity cosines $\approx$1.0
(fp32-accumulation readings marginally above 1 are numerical); late
layers are near-identity (identity fraction 0.93--0.97), so their
low top-64 subspace overlaps reflect noise-dominated residuals, not
disagreement. Readout stability: half-A/half-B eval pass@20 gaps
$\le$0.015 on every set --- far inside the 0.10 margin. \textbf{No
FIT-SENSITIVE classification; the merged lens is the OLMo primary.}

\subsection{OLMo causal core (v2 scoring throughout)}

\textbf{Verbal report}: category-equal top-1 \olvrcattopone{}, top-5
\olvrcattopfive{} (\olvrnexec{} executed; \olvrimproved{} improved /
\olvrworsened{} worsened). This is an order of magnitude above Qwen's
v1 numbers (v2 rerun pending) though far below the paper's 88\%
(Claude). \textbf{Flexible generalization}: capable top-1
\olfgcapaone{} ($\alpha{=}1$) $\to$ \olfgcapatwo{} ($\alpha{=}2$) ---
numerically indistinguishable from Qwen (5.8\%/0.0\%), \emph{including
the $\alpha{=}2$ reversal}: the over-strength overshoot is a
cross-model regularity of the paper-literal swap on open models,
whereas Sonnet 4.5 improved 76/192$\to$101/192. \textbf{Probe-swap raw
arm}: capable top-1 \olpscaptopone{} (diagnostic \olpsdiagtopone{};
\olpsncap{} capable of 90; paper 60\%).

\section{Extended battery (Groups A--C, both lanes)}

\begin{figure}[h]\centering
\includegraphics[width=\textwidth]{or1f08_battery_qwen.pdf}\\[2pt]
\includegraphics[width=\textwidth]{or1f08_battery_olmo.pdf}
\caption{\label{fig:battery}Battery overview, Qwen (top) and OLMo
(bottom): modulation contrast, dual-task reachability, ignition
transition width by pair family, introspection dose-response.}
\end{figure}

\textbf{Reproduced on both lanes.} Selectivity-language: the released
readout contrast is \emph{perfect on both models} (explicit 1.00 vs
automatic 0.00). Directed modulation: focus $>$ suppress $>0$ with the
white-bear residue (Qwen .72/.26; OLMo .44/.06; ``mention'' controls
pattern with focus, as expected when the instruction itself names the
target). Ignition: real concept pairs switch far more sharply than
idiom controls (Qwen .035 vs .209; OLMo .040 vs .100); the
depth-profile differs (Qwen narrows monotonically into the output;
OLMo is sharpest mid-band).

\textbf{Qwen-only.} Dual-task interference is present and asymmetric
(math 31\% $\gg$ concept 7\%). On OLMo the math cell is
\emph{capability-gated} --- single-task math reachability is 4.8\%, so
the interference estimand is missing, not zero; concept interference is
minimal (2.4\%).

\textbf{Null on both lanes.} Verbal introspection shows no
dose-response anywhere on the reconstructed ladder $\{0,1,2,4,8,16\}$
(OLMo's steered median RR is exactly 0); top-down summoning's
Q2$-$Q1 readout contrast is 0.0 on both lanes (7 items). Capacity
(descriptive): $\sim$2.9 (Qwen) / 1.6 (OLMo) list words at band-rank
$\le$5 at the end of 80-word lists ($\sim$8.2 / 4.6 at $\le$20).
Line-break family: R2 corpus-empty under the pinned filter (recorded
gap). Selectivity-linecount: rare rank-1 canon presence with weak
condition ordering in the paper direction on both lanes.

\section{Instrument cross-over (OR-Q4)}

\begin{figure}[h]\centering
\includegraphics[width=0.98\textwidth]{or1f09_crossover.pdf}
\caption{\label{fig:xo}The frozen 30-item official probe-swap subset
under both intervention families. Broad protected top-10 J-ablation
(campaign machinery, campaign band, g-folded dictionaries) knocks the
released answer out of top-1 on 14/30 (Qwen) and 5/19 (OLMo)
top-1-capable items versus $\le$1/30 and 1/19 for exact rank/energy
matched controls; paper-literal coordinate swaps complete the flip on
only 10--27\%.}
\end{figure}

Three OR-Q4 facts. (1) \emph{Intervention semantics dominate}: on the
same released prompts, broad J-space suppression is selectively
destructive while two-coordinate substitution rarely completes ---
Route~E's sentence is licensed: \textbf{the two interventions estimate
different causal questions}. (2) \emph{Population moderates}: the
campaign's C1-style ablation selectivity, established on campaign
banks, reappears on the official prompt population on both lanes ---
Route~F's moderator sentence is licensed. (3) \emph{The lens is not
the explanation}: the freshly fitted OR1 lens and the frozen campaign
lens agree under both families on OLMo (swap 10.0\% vs 10.0\%;
ablation 5/19 vs 6/19), and on Qwen the swap is if anything
\emph{stronger} on the campaign band (26.7\% vs 16.7\%) --- band and
fit choices do not rescue the paper-literal operation.

\section{Interpretation under the wording router (two lanes)}

Conformance and admission passed mechanically on both lanes (exact
parity, exact no-ops, verified pins; fit stability inside every
margin), so all results above are scientific observations about
model/instrument cells, not harness states.

The two lanes \textbf{dissociate the readout and intervention
properties}. On Qwen the J-lens readout advantage reproduces exactly as
the paper describes (multihop/multilingual profiles), yet paper-literal
swaps barely move behavior. On OLMo the readout advantage largely
\emph{disappears} (logit lens already strong in-band; near-identity
$J_\ell$), yet verbal report shows the strongest open-model swap effect
so far (25.5\% top-5). Meanwhile flexible generalization behaves
identically on both lanes ($\approx$5\% capable at $\alpha{=}1$, 0\% at
$\alpha{=}2$) --- the $\alpha{=}2$ reversal is a shared open-model
regularity that inverts the paper's Sonnet finding. The g-folding
asymmetry (material on Qwen, immaterial on OLMo) marks a concrete
basis-choice difference between the campaign's instruments and the
paper's, live on exactly the lane where interventions are weakest.

\textbf{Terminal routed sentences} (plan \S16.2; the complete
per-property accounting is the \S16.1 grid,
\texttt{reports/HEADLINE\_GRID.md}):

\begin{itemize}\itemsep2pt
\item \textbf{Readout properties} (lens quality, selectivity,
modulation, ignition, dual-task): a property-specific Route~A ---
multiple released readout contrasts reproduce directionally on both
open models at development tier, with selectivity-language exact on
both.
\item \textbf{Coordinate-intervention core} (verbal report, flexible
generalization, probe-swap): Route~D --- the released battery does not
reproduce the paper's core directional effects cleanly on the tested
open-model cells despite mechanically validated readout and
intervention implementations; effects are concordant across lanes but
sit at 5--30\% where the paper reports 40--88\%, and the paper's
$\alpha{=}2$ remedy inverts. This is a model/generalization result
bounded to the public release and reconstructed methods, not a
refutation of the Claude findings.
\item \textbf{Cross-over}: Routes E$+$F --- targeted substitution and
broad protected suppression estimate different causal questions, and
task population is a major moderator; the campaign's suppression
selectivity extends to the official prompts on both lanes while
lens-fit differences explain nothing.
\item \textbf{Report channel} (introspection, top-down): the
reconstructed protocols yield nulls on both lanes; because the
strength ladder is reconstructed rather than released (R1),
instrument-limitation is not excluded.
\end{itemize}

No workspace-existence or -absence claim is licensed for either model;
no frozen campaign claim is regraded; Claude magnitudes remain
descriptive context throughout.
